title: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Private Access

blocks.text: This guide takes you through the configuration steps that you must complete to begin using Private Access for your organization.
Before you configure Private Access, Zscaler recommends reading the following articles:

blocks.item: Signing In to the Zscaler Admin Console, including:

blocks.text: To configure Private Access, you must complete the following steps:

blocks.item: Step 1: Update Company and Administrator Information
To update your company information and configure administrators as applicable, see the following articles:

Private Access uses certificates to authenticate the App Connector and the user's device before each connection, as well as provide access to web applications via internet browser. To configure your certificates, see the following articles:
To learn more, see Certificate Management.

Private Access supports single sign-on (SSO) via SAML so that your remote users can access enterprise applications without having to log in separately to Private Access. To configure SSO for Private Access, see the following articles:
Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On
Step 4: Configure the Zscaler Client Connector
Installed on the user's device, Zscaler Client Connector connects to the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) to enable granular, policy-based access to your organization's internal resources.
To configure Zscaler Client Connector for your organization, see the following articles:
Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler Client Connector
Also refer to the following platform-specific Zscaler Client Connector articles:
Using Zscaler Client Connector for Windows
Using Zscaler Client Connector for macOS

App Connectors are lightweight virtual machines (VM) that you must configure in the data centers or virtual private clouds (VPC) that host your application servers. When the App Connectors are configured, they can connect to the ZTE to provide users with access to applications. To configure your App Connectors, see the following articles:
App Connector Deployment Guides for Supported Platforms
To learn more, see App Connector Management.
You must configure the applications you want to make accessible to your users via Private Access. To configure applications, see the following articles:
To learn more, see Application Management.
You can configure SAML attributes that you can then use when configuring policies. To configure your SAML attributes, see the following articles:
To learn more, see SAML Attributes.
Your users cannot access applications until you configure policies for them. To configure access and timeout policies, see the following articles:

The Log Streaming Service (LSS) provides a better understanding of the information coming from the Private Access service, by allowing you to create log receivers that obtain information about App Connectors and users. To configure your log receivers, see the following articles:
To learn more, see Log Streaming Service.
You can configure user portals for your organization that display links to applications that your users are allowed to access. To configure user portals, see the following articles:
Viewing and Managing Zscaler Client Connector Download Links
About User Portal Acceptable Use Policy
To learn more, see User Portal.
